rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial noun for an occasion of people fighting, especially a brawl.

example.english: Those two people were fighting in the street.
example.jyutping: go2 loeng5 go3 jan4 hai2 gaai1 dou6 daa2 gaa3

rows.note: Use this for organized combat or battle rather than an everyday fight.

example.english: The soldiers kept fighting on the front line for several days.
example.traditional: 士兵喺前線戰鬥咗幾日。
example.jyutping: si6 bing1 hai2 cin4 sin3 zin3 dau3 zo2 gei2 jat6

rows.note: Use this for conflict between people or groups rather than a physical fight itself.

example.english: There was fighting between the two departments over resource allocation.
example.traditional: 兩個部門因為資源分配問題有衝突。
example.jyutping: loeng5 go3 bou6 mun4 jan1 wai6 zi1 jyun4 fan1 pui3 man6 tai4 jau5 cung1 dat6

rows.note: Use this when the focus is violence as a method or feature of the fighting.

example.english: There is too much fighting and violence in this film, so I do not want the children to watch it.
example.traditional: 呢套戲暴力場面太多，我唔想畀細路睇。
example.jyutping: ni1 tou3 hei3 bou6 lik6 coeng4 min6 taai3 do1 ngo5 m4 soeng2 bei2 sai3 lou6 tai2
